# Classifiers

Classifiers map features to logits over a discrete vocabulary: untied and tied linear classifiers, the harmonic field, the crystal distance classifier, and the prismatic compositions of them, whose gate-combined parallel arms split the bias and variance axes. Multi-token prediction modules are a separate registry, ``mtp``; continuous-output modules live in ``generators``.

Namespace: ``registry.namespace("classifiers")``, declared in ``praxis.classifiers`` (17 entries)

Selected with ``--classifier-type`` (default: ``forward``).

## `crystal` - CrystalClassifier

Distance-based classifier (harmonic loss).

In encoder-attached mode the classifier sizes its centers to match the encoder's output
layout (so the distance computation lives in the encoder's feature space) and replaces
the encoder's dot-product projection at the loss boundary.

Source: [praxis/classifiers/crystal.py:309](../praxis/classifiers/crystal.py#L309)

## `crystal_harmonic`, `crystal_harmonic_static` - SequentialClassifier

Chain of classifiers: transforms compose, the last one classifies.

``stages`` is a list of builders (classifier class / ``partial`` over one) that are
instantiated with ``(config, encoder)``; already-built classifiers are accepted too (for
direct use).

Source: [praxis/classifiers/sequential.py:34](../praxis/classifiers/sequential.py#L34)

Presets:
- `crystal_harmonic` (`stages=[functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.harmonic.HarmonicClassifier'>, amp_modulation='off', build_scorer=False, fast_weights=False), <class 'praxis.classifiers.crystal.CrystalClassifier'>]`) - A harmonic field feeding the crystal distance classifier, composed by SequentialClassifier. The field is the bare grid (``amp_modulation="off"``) and is transform-only, so it allocates no dead scorer.
- `crystal_harmonic_static` (`stages=[functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.harmonic.HarmonicClassifier'>, amp_modulation='static', build_scorer=False, fast_weights=False), <class 'praxis.classifiers.crystal.CrystalClassifier'>]`) - crystal_harmonic with a fixed single oscillation on the field's envelope (``amp_modulation="static"``).

## `forward` - LinearClassifier

Standard next-token prediction classifier.

Its scorer is a single linear projection sized to :meth:`output_dims` - ``(hidden_size,
vocab_size)`` standalone, or the encoder's declared byte-output layout in encoder mode.
Builds nothing only when the encoder owns its full output pipeline (``handles_loss``,
e.g. CALM).

Source: [praxis/classifiers/linear.py:11](../praxis/classifiers/linear.py#L11)

## `harmonic` - HarmonicClassifier

Learnable linear scorer with a 2D harmonic field modulating features.

Owns both the field and the scorer, sized to :meth:`output_dims` (the encoder's declared
byte-output layout in encoder mode, else ``(hidden_size, vocab_size)``). ``forward``
modulates the features with the field, then projects through ``scorer`` - identical in
standalone and encoder modes.

Source: [praxis/classifiers/harmonic.py:1504](../praxis/classifiers/harmonic.py#L1504)

Gate-combined parallel branches; a SequentialClassifier stage or the top classifier.

Source: [praxis/classifiers/parallel.py:130](../praxis/classifiers/parallel.py#L130)

Branch 0 is a harmonic field with a learned but static envelope, read out by a plain linear classifier: the bias arm, a strong structural prior. Pair with ``loss_func: halo``: the loss detects the arm and runs its composite mode (mixture CE for the gate and the other arms, pure HALO geometry for this one). The control for the one choice prismatic6 makes beyond arm count: against prismatic6 it attributes any delta to the merge rather than to the shared stem.
- `prismatic7` (`branches=[<class 'praxis.classifiers.crystal.CrystalSmearClassifier'>, <class 'praxis.classifiers.linear.LinearClassifier'>, functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.halo.HaloClassifier'>, detach_in_blend=False)], stem=functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.harmonic.HarmonicClassifier'>, amp_modulation='input', build_scorer=False, fast_weights=True)`) - prismatic6's arms with the crystal bank merged the way the SMEAR paper merges: per example rather than on the batch mean, over one shared geometry plus low-rank deviations rather than N independent center sets (CrystalSmearClassifier). A batch-mean merge makes a constant router the design's fixed point, which ``smear_input_dependence`` near 0 shows. Identical to prismatic6 at initialization (LoRA init) and in its other two arms, so the swap is a clean A/B.
- `prismatic8` (`branches=[<class 'praxis.classifiers.crystal.CrystalClassifier'>, <class 'praxis.classifiers.linear.LinearClassifier'>, functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.halo.HaloClassifier'>, detach_in_blend=False)], stem=functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.harmonic.HarmonicClassifier'>, amp_modulation='input', build_scorer=False, fast_weights=True)`) - prismatic7 with the crystal bank collapsed to a single CrystalClassifier reading the shared stem. The trunk has already routed features at every level it offers - depth, residual, attention, memory - so a classifier that also picks its own geometry per example makes the last stage the least predictable one, which defeats the point of a distance classifier. The three arms give the classifier its choice; each arm is a fixed function of the stem, and ``causal_readout`` holds on the geometric arm. The other two arms match prismatic7, so the comparison isolates the bank.

## `prismatic10`, `prismatic9` - SurgicalParallelClassifier

ParallelClassifier whose arms train on their own objectives, combined by PCGrad.

Identical to ParallelClassifier in the forward pass and at inference: the same mixture
of softmaxes over the same arms, so nothing about how predictions are made changes. What
changes is training, and only training.

The honest cost, stated up front: solo cross-entropy on every arm removes the DIVISION
OF LABOUR. Under the mixture, arms specialize - each covers what it explains best and
the gate routes ...

Source: [praxis/classifiers/parallel.py:970](../praxis/classifiers/parallel.py#L970)

Presets:
- `prismatic10` (`branches=[<class 'praxis.classifiers.crystal.CrystalClassifier'>, <class 'praxis.classifiers.crystal.CrystalClassifier'>]`) - Two CrystalClassifiers reading the trunk directly: no harmonic stem and no HALO arm, trained as prismatic9 trains its arms. Each arm learns from its own harmonic cross-entropy, the trunk from their PCGrad-combined gradient, and the gate from the mixture. The arms differ only by initialization, so the gate's split and arm_cos_01 say whether two geometries are worth more than one.
- `prismatic9` (`branches=[<class 'praxis.classifiers.crystal.CrystalClassifier'>, <class 'praxis.classifiers.linear.LinearClassifier'>, functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.halo.HaloClassifier'>, detach_in_blend=False)], stem=functools.partial(<class 'praxis.classifiers.harmonic.HarmonicClassifier'>, amp_modulation='input', build_scorer=False, fast_weights=True)`) - prismatic8's three arms, trained differently: each arm gets its own cross-entropy instead of the mixture's residual, and the trunk receives one PCGrad-combined gradient over those three objectives rather than their plain sum. The blend is unchanged and still makes every prediction; it stops deciding how much each arm is trained. The cost is the division of labour: arms trained alone all learn the whole task, and val NLL is where that shows. See SurgicalParallelClassifier and _pcgrad in praxis/classifiers/parallel.py.

## `tied` - TiedClassifier

Classifier with tied weights. Instead of having a separate output projection, this
classifier reuses the embedding weights for the output layer.

Source: [praxis/classifiers/tied.py:13](../praxis/classifiers/tied.py#L13)
